title: E2E: Hosted canary rollout workflow (create/start/step/pause/rollback + approvals)
author: Leila Farouk
description: Context: As part of Hosted canary rollouts GA, we need reliable end-to-end coverage across Console → orchestrator → policy engine → routing enforcement → telemetry. This PR adds Playwright-based E2E tests that exercise the happy path and the high-risk control paths (pause/rollback, approvals required, and SLO auto-stop). The suite is written to run in CI against the shared staging environment using dedicated test tenants/routes, and is structured to minimize flakiness (deterministic cohorting assertions, eventual consistency waits, and tighter network mocking where appropriate). Scope: (1) Create rollout via Console wizard: pick Hosted route, select baseline vs canary model version, define traffic schedule (1% → 5% → 25%), configure guardrails. (2) Start rollout and validate routing split enforcement: verify request cohort assignment stickiness and that approximate canary traffic matches config within tolerance (per region + aggregate). (3) Progress steps with soak-time handling: verify step cannot be advanced before min soak unless privileged override; verify audit activity entries appear for each action. (4) Pause and resume: verify can pause during a soak, traffic split freezes, and resume continues from the paused step. (5) Rollback: verify rollback sets split back to 0% canary and routes to baseline; confirm activity timeline shows rollback action and reason. (6) Approval-required flow: verify policy engine blocks step change without approver; verify approver user can approve; verify audit log event emitted with actor + diff. (7) Auto-stop/rollback wiring (smoke): simulate SLO breach signal via test-only metrics hook and assert rollout transitions to paused/rollback per policy, and the UI shows the stop reason. Notes/assumptions: - Uses TEST_ONLY endpoints guarded behind env var + allowlisted tenant to set synthetic metrics and accelerate soak time in staging CI. - Makes no assertions about chart rendering details (covered by unit tests); instead asserts the underlying cohort metrics API returns expected series labels and non-empty values. - All tests tag created rollouts with run_id and perform cleanup to reduce test pollution. Follow-ups: - Expand multi-region coverage to include ap-southeast during GA hardening (blocked on staging capacity). - Add “retry + streaming request” cohort stickiness test once streaming retry semantics land (see ADR cohorting + PR-28741).
commits: test(e2e): add rollout fixtures + test tenant bootstrap
test(e2e): create+start rollout wizard happy path
test(e2e): step progression w/ min soak + override gating
test(e2e): synthetic SLO breach hook + auto-stop assertion
ci(e2e): shard rollouts suite + tighten retries for known flakes
chore: cleanup helpers + docs for running locally
review_conversation: Dylan Brooks: This is the coverage we needed for GA. Two questions: (1) can we avoid relying on chart UI selectors? (2) what’s the expected tolerance on traffic split assertions? Leila Farouk (author): (1) Yep—updated to assert cohort metrics API payload + the presence of the cohort labels instead of reading chart DOM. UI selectors are now only for wizard navigation + action buttons. (2) Added helper assertSplitApprox(split, tolerance=0.08) with min sample size guard; in staging we send 400 requests per step, so tolerance is stable. Chloe Martin: I’m a bit nervous about the TEST_ONLY metrics hook. Is it tenant-allowlisted and off by default? Leila Farouk: Yes—guarded behind ROLLOUT_TEST_ONLY_HOOKS=1 and allowlists the e2e tenant id; endpoints return 404 otherwise. Also added a unit test to ensure the allowlist check is enforced. Mina Haddad: For routing enforcement, the test currently hits a single region. Can we at least validate that the cohort key stays sticky across retries? Leila Farouk: Added a stickiness assertion where the same request_id hashed key stays canary/baseline across 20 requests; for cross-region we still only assert aggregate because staging doesn’t have consistent ap-southeast capacity in CI. Added follow-up note in description. Sean Gallagher: Please add guardrails to prevent alert spam in staging (we’ve seen e2e cause noisy dashboards). Leila Farouk: Updated the synthetic breach to use the test-only signal path that does not emit customer-facing alerts; it only flips orchestrator state. Also added tags rollout_test_run=true so we can filter dashboards. Connor O'Brien: CI flaked twice on the step soak wait. Can we reduce wall time and tighten eventual waits? Leila Farouk: Changed to use accelerated soak in staging (test-only) and replaced fixed sleeps with eventually() polling + deadline. Reduced suite runtime from ~18m to ~9m. Chloe Martin: One more: approvals flow should verify audit event actor + diff. Leila Farouk: Added assertion that activity timeline includes APPROVAL_GRANTED with actor email and step_percent change diff. Approved. Mina Haddad: Approved with the note that we should add streaming retry coverage later. Sean Gallagher: Approved; thanks for the staging noise guard. Dylan Brooks: LGTM. Merge after green.
timeline: 2025-04-22 — PR opened by Leila Farouk; initial suite added for create/start/step/pause/rollback. 2025-04-24 — First CI run shows flake in soak-time step progression; rerun passes; reviewers request eventual waits + reduced reliance on UI selectors. 2025-04-25 — Added metrics API assertions and replaced sleep with polling; introduced test-only accelerated soak and allowlist guard for staging. 2025-04-26 — Added approval-required flow assertions including audit timeline diff/actor checks; sharded CI workflow. 2025-04-28 — All checks green; approvals from Console, Routing, and SRE; merged via squash.
release_notes: Internal: Adds GA-critical E2E coverage for Hosted canary rollout workflow including approvals and rollback paths; improves confidence in routing split enforcement and orchestrator policy wiring.
